plugins.name: isolated-review
plugins.description: TAKT-based isolated code review. Runs each review perspective (correctness, regression, tests, security + overall) as an independent read-only session, consolidates findings in a dedicated integration session, and formats the result without changing verdicts.

plugins.name: light-review
plugins.description: Cognitive-load-light PR review. Findings are written as an inverted pyramid — one-line conclusion, minimal evidence, the fix, the impact, what still needs checking — with the severity-swinging context embedded in the finding itself; the spots confirmed OK keep the full waterfall so the reasons for approval stay on record. Code-smell centric, no TAKT.

plugins.name: health-checkup
plugins.description: Periodic repository health checkup. Counts — never blocks — the obligations offloaded during development: unresolved TODOs, "guaranteed elsewhere" claims classified as verified / missing / untraceable, stale and unmilestoned issues, coverage, and spec-implementation drift. An LLM only extracts where a claim points; scripts decide whether that place exists and append the numbers next to their baselines, leaving the diagnosis to humans.

plugins.name: draft-review-loop
plugins.description: Orchestration loops that carry automatically generated PRs out of the queue. They own the ordering, the repetition and its ceilings, and the exit — not the review itself, which is delegated to light-review / isolated-review. codex-draft-review takes a codex-authored draft PR to human-review-ready: acceptance criteria read thickly at the entrance and confirmed at the exit, verification placed immediately after every loop that changes code, and no merge — the verdict stays with the human. bot-pr-resolve takes a Dependabot / Renovate / security PR off the queue: classify the route, inspect the actual change and CI, and merge only when every safety criterion holds, otherwise hand it over with the blocking criterion named. One PR per invocation; the outer iteration belongs to /loop.

plugins.name: worker-fleet
plugins.description: Supervisor-side loop that keeps a fleet of Claude worker sessions busy. One tick sweeps every worker: it answers approval prompts (everything except merge, which goes to the human), nudges the ones that have gone silent, advances the ones that finished, and starts one new worker in a free slot from a labeled issue. Capacity is re-measured every tick from free memory and CPU rather than fixed at startup, and silence is classified rather than assumed to mean done. Workers run Claude — not codex — because the work happens on top of openspec-workflow's delta specs, tasks, and fixup flow. The implementation belongs to openspec-workflow and the review to draft-review-loop; this plugin owns capacity, classification, intervention, and dispatch.
